CONTROL 3 -- truncation. Cutting each Green column at radius R turns the locality claim

TWO different questions, which the first version conflated into one number:
norm inside R   how much of the field's L2 norm a truncated support carries
peak inside R   how much of the LARGEST displacement it carries
A response can be local in amplitude and global in norm -- a small floor spread over 13,000
atoms carries as much norm as a sharp peak over 100 -- and those need different answers.

The identity holds. One factorisation at 25 s makes every subsequent response a
89 ms solve, and every EVENT a 83 us addition over a
4970-atom support. The 11.4-year figure was the cost of repeatedly computing something
already known. What this cannot absorb is nonlinearity: a contact, a melting bubble or a
topology change alters K itself, which invalidates the factors and the columns with them.
